mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lynronne-1 preferentially binds/folds in anionic bacterial-mimetic membranes and detergent micelles while showing little association with zwitterionic mammalian-mimetic membranes.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism is demonstrated in model membranes and micelles, not directly in bacterial cells.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lynronne-1 disrupts anionic POPC:POPG vesicles more strongly than POPC vesicles in carboxyfluorescein leakage assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is a model-vesicle lysis assay; it supports membrane disruption but not a direct cellular pore structure.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Changing the hydrophobic helical face produces the expected lysis/activity continuum, with R4L S8L showing stronger lytic and antimicrobial activity and I10T V15T the weakest activity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Lynronne-1 variants R4L S8L, V15T, and I10T V15T
mechanism_claims.limitations: The relationship is source-supported for the tested variants only; it should not be generalized to untested substitutions.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper favors a detergent/carpet-style membrane lysis model over pore formation for Lynronne-1 based on helix length, lipid selectivity, and model-vesicle lysis behavior.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: wild-type Lynronne-1 and R4L S8L model
mechanism_claims.limitations: The carpet-model assignment remains an interpretation from biophysical evidence; it is not a directly visualized cellular mechanism.

quality_controls.note: Every direct_mechanism claim has direct_assay_types; the carpet-model claim is kept as inferred_mechanism.

adjudication_note: Worker-6 replaced automated mechanism locator notes with source-reviewed mechanism claims and preserved the carpet model as inferred rather than directly proven.
